name: Crawler Leg
summary: Along Darkshore’s misty coast, crabs lose legs that most travelers have no use for. Their tough limbs can help keep a gnome’s communication device working.

sections.title: Gnomish Ingenuity on the Coast
sections.body: Darkshore’s crabs leave sturdy limbs along the shore, from pygmy tide crawlers to reef crawlers. Night elf sentinels pay them little mind, but the gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle has found a use for them. Working from Auberdine, Wizbang designed his prototype long-distance communication devices, called buzzboxes, to run on improvised local components. Crawler legs’ segmented joints and durable chitin provide the friction and leverage needed to repair Buzzbox 827, along the shoreline just south of town.

faq.q: What are crawler legs used for?
faq.answer: Crawler legs are gathered to repair Buzzbox 827, an experimental communication station along the Darkshore coast just south of Auberdine. Gnome inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle placed it there.

faq.q: Where do crawler legs come from?
faq.answer: Crawler legs come from crabs along the beaches of Darkshore, including Pygmy Tide Crawlers, Young Reef Crawlers, Encrusted Tide Crawlers, and Reef Crawlers.

faq.q: Why does a mechanical buzzbox need crab legs?
aliases: how does crawler leg fix buzzbox
faq.answer: Wizbang Cranktoggle designed his machines to use parts from nearby wildlife for field repairs. Crawler legs’ rigid joints and chitinous segments fit the grinding gears of the buzzbox and restore its mechanisms.

angles.text: Wizbang Cranktoggle’s use of crab legs as makeshift levers shows gnomish field improvisation, substituting nearby materials for standard metal linkages.
As a gnome, you may see aggressive crustaceans on a beach and recognize their legs as possible parts for a delicate long-distance communication network.
